articles.title: Salah 'destroza' al Galatasaray
articles.standfirst: El 'hat-trick' del egipcio comandó la goleada del Trabzonspor ante el vigente campeón de la Superliga turca
articles.summary: El 'hat-trick' del egipcio comandó la goleada del Trabzonspor ante el vigente campeón de la Superliga turca
articles.body: Mohamed Salah ha caído de pie en Turquía. Fue recibido como un auténtico mito por parte de los aficionados de Trabzonspor y se bañó en gloria 'destrozando' a un Galatasaray invicto hasta la fecha (4-0) con un 'hat-trick'. No habían transcurrido ni cinco minutos y ya había dejado su sello en el partido. De manera incomprensible, la defensa del Galatasaray estaba volcada en campo rival y salió como una 'flecha' para definir mano a mano ante Çakir. Pasan los años. Pero todavía sigue teniendo 'chispa'. Trabzonspor, prácticamente, no volvió a acercarse por la portería rival. Pero, en cuestión de cinco minutos, Salah le regaló una asistencia a Saviolo y celebró su doblete a pase de Franculino para materializar el 3-0 antes de poner dirección al túnel de vestuarios. Okan Buruk, completamente desesperado, perdió los papeles a 20' para el final y acabó expulsado. Salah, por su parte, todavía se guardaba una última carta y firmó su doblete en el 80'. En apenas seis jornadas de Superliga turca, ya ha generado nueve goles con la camiseta del Trabzonspor. Ugochukwu, para 'redondear' la noche, también vio la roja.

articles.title: Celtic win over Rangers 'changes game', says Scott Brown before Old Firm derby
articles.summary: Former Celtic captain Scott Brown believes a win for the Scottish champions against Rangers on Sunday "changes the game" after a turbulent week for Martin O'Neill's side.
articles.body:
Former Celtic captain Scott Brown believes a win for the Scottish champions against Rangers on Sunday "changes the game" after a turbulent week for Martin O'Neill's side.

Rangers triumphed 3-0 at home in last Sunday's Old Firm League Cup quarter-final before Celtic opened their Europa League campaign with a 3-1 defeat at home by Ferencvaros on Thursday.

However, Celtic's early season domestic form has them going into Sunday's match in the east end of Glasgow - which like last week will have no visiting supporters in attendance - with a five-point advantage over their Ibrox rivals.

"If Celtic win and they're eight points clear, it changes the game," Brown said on BBC Scotland's YouTube channel.

"Can [Rangers] go to Celtic Park and do they exact same thing as last week?

"Celtic now have had a week to understand how that game went. They are going to have to make sure that they match that energy but also match that willingness to go and win the match."

Celtic seek spark as Rangers aim for further derby joy

Listen on Sportsound, highlights on Sportscene

20/9/26 from 11:00 BST (radio), 19:15 (TV)

McInnes got it right last week - can O'Neill respond?

Brown was impressed by Rangers manager Derek McInnes' change of approach in the season's first derby, change to a 3-5-2 shape and going man for man with Celtic's front three.

"They went after Celtic from the get go," Brown said. "They looked like they wanted the win more. For him to change his tactics, nobody expected him to do that. That is a very, very good manager to pick that out."

Brown also pondered Celtic's tactical plan.

"Martin O'Neill when he was manager [from 2000-05], loved a 3-5-2 and it was fantastic to watch," said the former Scotland captain.

"He had two big guys up front. That was an unbelievable team. He's not got those players that probably can be suited to a 3-5-2."

With Yang Hyun-jun still on Asian Games duty with South Korea, Sebastian Tounekti and James Forrest have both been used on Celtic's left flank.

But Brown believes the club's problems go beyond that.

"Rangers got in their face, they blocked Callum McGregor off and as soon as you block Callum McGregor off and you man-mark Cal, it's hard for anyone else to go and dictate.

"That's when you need a [Benjamin] Nygren to drop under, a [Mika] Baur to go and drop under and them do their job as well. You can't always keep looking at Cal to do everything."

And Brown believes who starts best could be crucial.

"Rangers were up for the fight," he added on Sportsound. "The first 15 minutes, it should be a battle. If you can go and win that battle, you can get the ball down.

"Celtic started very, very slow last week. They need to go back to basics, make sure they've got the fight, make sure they've got the hunger because they've got the talent - I know they've got the talent.

"You cannot have just one of those days against your biggest rivals, ever."

articles.title: Nottingham Forest 0-1 Coventry: Jay Dasilva's winner gives Sky Blues first Premier League win in 25 years
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Coventry earn first Premier League win of season with 1-0 victory at Nottingham Forest; Jay Dasilva's second-half winner ends Sky Blues' 25-year wait for top-flight goal and win; Forest saw Igor Jesus' late equaliser controversially disallowed by VAR
articles.body:
Frank Lampard's side needed a late VAR intervention to end their long wait for victory after Forest substitute Igor Jesus saw an 86th-minute equaliser ruled out.

Referee Jarred Gillett was sent to the pitchside monitor, where he adjudged Jesus had fouled Caleb Yirenkyi before finishing from close range inside the area.

Questioned on the incident, Lampard told Sky Sports : "As you see on the replay, he has that little step on him which puts him off balance, and it's a foul...I think that's VAR reaching the right decision."

Latest news and rumours: Forest | Coventry

It was the second goal Forest have had disallowed at home by VAR this season after Neco Williams had a goal chalked off in the 0-0 draw against Tottenham.

The latest controversial call meant Dasilva's 55th-minute goal, assisted by goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, ended the Sky Blues' pointless and goalless start to the season.

The visitors also needed a superb 76th-minute Bobby Thomas goalline clearance to deny Jesus an equaliser.

Forest's defeat means Oliver Glasner's side are yet to score or win at home in any competition this season, while they have won just once in the league at the City Ground since December last year.

Forest had 14 shots in the first half but were undone just 10 minutes after half-time as Rushworth's pinpoint long ball found Dasilva, who took a superb touch to beat Daniel Munoz before firing coolly beyond Matz Sels.

Dasilva's first goal in 127 Coventry appearances moves the Sky Blues off the foot of the table and inside the relegation zone only on goal difference, while Forest sit 12th.

Redknapp: Coventry showed they can do it in PL

"It's been a really hard start for them [Coventry], in terms of the teams they've had to play. But there were signs where they thought, 'we can compete at this level'.

"It was so important to get this win. I'm pleased for the players, the fans and obviously for Frank Lampard.

"They've done such a great job getting here, and now you want to make it count. You want to get rid of that inferiority complex. Can we handle the occasion and the Premier League? They showed that.

"They defended really well, looked dangerous on the break with some big performances."

Coventry boss Frank Lampard speaking at his post-match press conference:

"We have to keep our feet on the ground because it's one win, and we've felt how ruthless the league is already.

"We've had two of the toughest games on paper, probably in (Manchester) City and Arsenal, but it doesn't matter.

"The points still said zero after four games, and that hurts. So I think going into a break, yeah, for sure, for everyone to have a bit of rest, to feel good about it.

"You know that's the starting point, so they can use that.

"Every win is a relief, no matter what. I mean, especially in our position, because you sit at the bottom of the table, you want to win because you don't like to look at it.

"But even when you're top of the Championship last year, there's a version of a relief for the manager, anyway."

Glasner: Defeat is a result of 'heaviness from the past'

Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner speaking at his post-match press conference:

"For me, being very honest, I felt for the first time the heaviness of the past. The players were very quiet before the game.

"I just saw and felt that everybody, let's say, with a red shirt, got nervous today, and I think this is, for me now, and I'm still in the process of understanding the players, understanding Forest, maybe the biggest part of what we have to get under control, not to feel this pressure.

"Today we felt, 'ah, we have to win it now'. We play a promoted team at home. We have to win.

"We have to win, and we all know then some things don't work, and that's how I analyse the game.

"So, for me, the biggest problem was not the football skill; it was more the mental side, and that's why it's pretty clear now players need support here."

articles.title: Kilmarnock 1-1 Hearts: Stephen Kingsley strikes late to rescue Jambos point
articles.summary: Report as Hearts captain Stephen Kingsley scores an 86th-minute equaliser to rescue a 1-1 draw at Kilmarnock and lift the Jambos back above Rangers into second place on goal difference
articles.body:
The Jambos arrived at Rugby Park eager to banish a dismal display in Tuesday's 2-1 loss at Falkirk, but a 16th minute own goal from Jamie McCart, as he tried to challenge Killie forward Joe Hugill, left them chasing the game once again.

Hearts' second-half pressure eventually paid off when Kingsley fired home in the 86th minute to lift them back into second place on goal difference from Rangers, but Wouter Vrancken's side will be frustrated with a return of just one point from two favourable fixtures before the three-week break.

Killie boss Neil McCann made two changes to the side that picked up a first league win of the season at Hibernian on Tuesday as injured goalkeeper Max Stryjek and on-loan Hearts defender MJ Kamson-Kamara were replaced by Calum Ferrie and Jamie Brandon.

There were three changes to the Hearts team that lost at Falkirk in midweek as Christian Borchgrevink, Kingsley and Tomas Magnusson were all added, while record signing Ageu was on the bench for the first time since suffering a long-term injury in February.

Hearts thought they had gone ahead in the 11th minute when Kingsley's cross was forced in by a combination of Laurent Mendy and Killie defender Cathal McCarthy. Following a VAR check, however, the goal was ruled out for handball by Mendy.

It proved pivotal as the hosts went ahead five minutes later. Michael Schjonning-Larsen's clipped ball over the top sent Hugill clear and Hearts defender McCart, chasing back, prodded the ball past his own keeper Beau Reus as he slid in to challenge the forward 12 yards out.

Moments after Claudio Braga flashed an effort just wide for Hearts, boss Vrancken, who looked exasperated with his side's general lack of urgency in possession, made the bold call to replace centre-back Stuart Findlay with Harry Milne in the 32nd minute.

The change seemed to have a positive effect as the visitors looked more threatening towards the interval, with chances for James Wilson, Braga, Milne and Josh McPake in the last 10 minutes of the half.

Vrancken made a triple change just before the hour, as Ageu, Sabri Guendouz and JJ Williams were all introduced, and Guendouz had three attempts from distance within 10 minutes of entering the fray while Miller saw an effort deflected just wide.

Williams then sent a close-range header over from a Sabah Kerjota corner as Hearts started to crank up the heat, and the equaliser eventually came in the 86th minute when Kingsley pounced to drill home a low shot after Kerjota's free-kick from the right broke to him eight yards out.

Hearts chased a winner in the closing moments but were unable to find a way through, with Williams going closest in stoppage time.

articles.title: Steve Evans: Bristol Rovers manager 'not going anywhere' amid Hibernian links
articles.summary: Bristol Rovers manager Steve Evans says he is 'not going anywhere' amid speculation linking him with the vacant role at Hibernian.
articles.body:
Bristol Rovers manager Steve Evans said his commitment remains with the League Two club amid speculation linking him with the vacant job at Hibernian.

Evans took over at the League Two club last December and after securing their safety in the fourth tier last season he signed a new contract in April to extend his agreement at the Memorial Stadium until 2028.

The Gas are sixth in the table, with four wins from their opening seven games, although suffered a second consecutive defeat with a 3-0 loss away to Gillingham on Saturday.

Evans said there has been "no contact" from Scottish Premiership side Hibernian, who sacked manager David Gray on 16 September, after six successive home defeats.

"I'm humbled to be linked to a job like that because if you're a Scotsman you know how big a football club that is but I'm not going anywhere," Evans told BBC Radio Bristol.

"I've come here to deliver on a project - it doesn't feel like that driving home this evening - but my commitment is to this football club."

The 63-year-old has never managed in his home country over his 32-year career in the dugout having spent his playing days with Clyde, Albion Rovers, Ayr United, Hamilton Academical and St Johnstone.

Evans is a lifelong Celtic fan and said there was "a certain team in Glasgow" that could take his career to Scotland.

"I've often maintained there's only one club that will take me to Scotland and, if they ever did ring, I'm in the car," he added.

"A certain team in Glasgow, there's only one team I would leave this for and of course my country because everyone would manage their country.

"I don't think I'll get either of those jobs now but that's the only team I'd go north of the border for."

articles.title: Everton unbeaten but David Moyes wants more - and won't talk about Europe
articles.summary: Fifth in the Premier League table and yet to lose this season, Everton are on the up, but boss David Moyes wants further improvements - and don't mention Europe.
articles.body:
Unbeaten after five games and fifth in the Premier League, Everton boss David Moyes is refusing to think of Europe after allowing himself to dream last season.

"We are not using those words this year," said Moyes bluntly after a 1-0 victory at home against Ipswich Town took the Toffees to nine points.

They have two wins and three draws from their first month of the campaign, a healthy start.

But the way 2025-26 ended for Everton was a painful experience for Moyes and the club's fans, and nobody will be getting ahead of themselves this time.

A 3-0 win over Chelsea in March had left Moyes' side eighth, three points off what would have been a Champions League place.

But just as the fans dreamed of a first European experience since 2017-18, the wheels came off with no wins in their final seven games.

Everton finished 13th, four points behind Brighton , who qualified for the Conference League, and five off Sunderland , who joined Bournemouth and Crystal Palace in the Europa League.

So it is no wonder Moyes is refusing to get carried away now.

Asked whether he had challenged his players to earn European qualification this season, Moyes said: "Not [saying] in front of you people [the media], that's for sure, because we're still preparing ourselves and make sure we can do the best we can.

"I enjoyed saying the words last year. If you think of what we had done, been relegation material when we came in January [2025], got out and won the games, 12/13 new players had to come in...

"But the players had done so well, I started to believe that we had a real chance, and it allowed me to be like that."

Resilient Everton show defensive strength again

Everton 's strong start, in which they have also won two Carabao Cup games to set up a home last-16 tie against Newcastle in October, had been based on a solid defence.

Moyes' side have kept five clean sheets in seven matches overall and got the three points against Ipswich thanks to an 11th-minute goal from Thierno Barry, his fifth of the season.

What makes Everton 's form even more impressive is the fact Barry is the only recognised striker at the club after Beto moved to Fiorentina on transfer deadline day, with key attacking midfielder Iliman Ndiaye joining Manchester City on the same day.

However, Moyes felt his side, one of only five still unbeaten in the Premier League, still have plenty of work to do before he will be happy.

"We've had draws at Tottenham and Bournemouth away from home and we've done pretty well," said Moyes. "Keeping clean sheets is something to be pleased about and try to build on.

"We've statistically been making more chances and we had 21 shots [against Ipswich], which is very good, but only two on target which isn't very good.

"The players get huge credit to get to this point, unbeaten in five games. It's really good, but I'm expecting them to do this.

"If we're thinking 'we're doing a great job because we've gone a few games', no, the manager expects that. I'm actually more disappointed that we aren't scoring more goals.

"I'm rapping them like you wouldn't believe - why are we not getting better crosses into the box, better finishes, shooting from the edge of the box, not scoring more? That's the only thing we're missing from being a half-decent side."

When Moyes returned for a second spell in charge of Everton in January 2025, the Toffees were 16th, one point clear of the relegation zone.

He has had to cope with rising expectations but was quick to point to the club's progress since he came back.

"I heard a lot of things [said] that last year was not so good and I thought 'my goodness, I don't know what the people are talking or writing about because it's absolute baloney'.

"It was fantastic what we did and we came so close to doing something that would have been incredibly special after no money, being on the verge of relegation, moving to a new stadium - and it has never been an easy job for anyone moving to a new stadium - so we came really close."

Assessing Everton 's unbeaten status, former England midfielder and BBC pundit Danny Murphy said: "Nothing surprises me with a David Moyes side.

"They're so well organised, so well motivated and always dangerous when their backs are against the wall. There's been a lot of discontent among the fanbase regarding the owners and a transfer policy that left themselves short in forward areas.

"But the rest of the side is so well balanced, they all know their jobs, they know what they're doing and that backline with the keeper behind it is really solid. So, I never thought it was a catastrophe that they didn't get a striker in.

"Because they're so well organised and defensively so good, they're always going to nick results when they're not playing well. I do understand the fans' frustration, but I didn't think for a second they'd be in any danger because they didn't get cover in for their forwards.

"It is a thin squad, but they've still got quality."

Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford told BBC Sport the result felt like a positive way to end this part of the season, with the international break meaning the Toffees are not in league action again until 11 October when they will face Hull City .

"You have to dig in, that's the Everton way," Pickford said. "We are building momentum and we will be focused and ready to go when we come back. It was a great way to finish the week off."

Looking at the contribution of goalscorer Barry, who found the net just eight times last season but now looks a greater threat, Pickford said: "He works hard and the goals will come from working hard. The first year in the Premier League is always tough. He has found his feet and he has started a lot better this year.

"It's always good to finish with a win, especially before a long international break."

articles.title: Giráldez: “La victoria nos viene bien para irnos con una sonrisa después de un mes duro”
articles.standfirst: El técnico celebra la goleada aunque no le gustó el primer tiempo
articles.summary: El técnico celebra la goleada aunque no le gustó el primer tiempo
articles.body: Claudio Giráldez se fue satisfecho con la goleada de su equipo, aunque el primer tiempo no le gustó, cree que les dará tranquilidad y agradece las muestras de apoyo de la grada aún no sintiéndose protagonista. Goleada que da tranquilidad: “Nos quejábamos un poco del calendario y ahora la sensación es que no queríamos que parase y menos tantas semanas. Va a venir bien para descansar, para irnos con una sonrisa por lo menos después de este mes duro en cuanto a calendario y en cuanto a resultados. La gente de dentro siempre ha confiado y tiene su recompensa hoy a mucho esfuerzo". No le gustó el primer tiempo: “Una primera parte mala, que ha sido de lo peor que hemos hecho este año. Nos vamos con un 2-0 y el fútbol tiene estas cosas a veces. A partir del 3-0 se desata el bote de ketchup y vemos a un equipo liberado, jugando muy rápido, muy bien, con muchas llegadas. Es excesivo el resultado. Nos iguala los goles que nos gustaría llevar pero simplemente son 7 puntos y hay que tener tranquilidad y calma”. Ambicioso: “No nos llega, queremos más. Por lo menos nos vamos con una alegría y para la gente que también lo estaba sufriendo y me alegro por ellos". Recuperar sensaciones: “Evidentemente los resultados no ayudaban a esa confianza pero creo que debemos tener más pose y tranquilidad con la pelota de la que hemos tenido. La segunda parte ellos cambian el sistema y nos ajustamos rápido. Con la entrada de los cambios creo que hemos mejorado, hemos tenido más tranquilidad”. Muestras de apoyo de la grada al técnico: “Yo me voy aliviado por la gente, no por mí. Insisto, creo que los resultados llegan desde trabajar, desde hacer cosas bien, desde darle al fútbol cosas, desde que el equipo crea en lo que hacemos o en lo que proponemos. Veo una convicción total del equipo. Es un alivio para toda la gente que estaba preocupada por cómo arrancamos. No es un buen arranque en cuanto a resultados, no hemos tenido la sensación de generar, finalizar o hacer goles que nos gustaría pero hemos hecho partidos para hacer muchos más goles que hoy”.

articles.summary: No logaron pasar del empate en casa ante el Excelsior (2.2)
articles.body: No termina de coger vuelo el Ajax de Míchel. Fue tomando temperatura el Ajax con el transcurso de la primera parte y, en el 32', Gloukh desbordó por banda izquierda para terminar metiendo un envío al interior del área convertido con sutileza por Julian Brandt. Tercer partido consecutivo marcando para el ex del Borussia Dortmund. Pudieron caer varios más para el Ajax antes del descanso. Pero, en el tiempo de descuento, Hartjes cazó un balón suelto y, a la media vuelta, batió a Ter Stegen. No se lo podía creer el Johan Cruyff Arena... así como el 1-2 convertido por Sliti cuando se acaba de superar la hora de partido. No estuvo acertado el propio Ter Stegen a la hora de cortar el centro de Yegoian. Reaccionó de inmediato el Ajax para enmendar el error del meta cedido por el Barcelona y Arokodare fue el encargado de firmar el 2-2 con el que finalizaría el partido. Kehrer, eso sí, se jugó el penalti en una de las últimas acciones del encuentro. articles.standfirst: El argentino reacciona con un 'Me gusta' a una publicación del Atlético pidiendo unión antes del encuentro ante el Real Madrid
articles.summary: El argentino reacciona con un 'Me gusta' a una publicación del Atlético pidiendo unión antes del encuentro ante el Real Madrid
articles.body: Julián Alvarez está volviendo por donde solía. Superado el trance del mercado de fichajes y la bronca de la afición el día de su regreso al Metropolitano en el encuentro ante el Villarreal, poco a poco las aguas se están calmando. El delantero argentino también rema para ello. Y está poniendo de su parte tanto dentro como fuera del terreno de juego. Rinde mejor en el césped, como demostró en el encuentro ante el Liverpool, firmando una buena actuación y una asistencia a Llorente, y pone de su parte en los entrenamientos. Muestra compromiso y se implica en el trabajo diario con el equipo. El delantero, arropado, sobre todo, por Kang-in Lee y por Cuti Romero, se ha esforzado para llegar a punto al derbi ante al Real Madrid. Julián, que se había perdido por lesión los dos últimos encuentros del Atlético ante Osasuna y Real Sociedad, ha trabajado duro para superar la sobrecarga muscular en el cuádriceps que le ha tenido de baja y entrar en la convocatoria para medirse a los de Mourinho este domingo. El argentino no solo está mostrando su implicación en el verde. También fuera del campo, públicamente en las redes sociales. Julián ha reaccionado esta tarde con un 'Me gusta' a una publicación del Atlético en Instagram. El club rojiblanco subió una serie de imágenes del estadio y de la afición con un mensaje claro de cara al derbi. "Mañana. Todos. Juntos.", se leía en el texto que acompañaba a las fotografías. Con su reacción, al igual que otros jugadores de la plantilla como Koke o Musso, el delantero da un paso más en su reconciliación y ofrece otra muestra de su compromiso con el equipo. A esa vuelta a la normalidad con el 'caso Julián' se refirió, antes del último encuentro ante Osasuna, Mateu Alemany, director de Fútbol Profesional Masculino del Atlético. "Eso ya hay que entenderlo y superarlo. Ha pasado lo que ha pasado, pero ha vuelto, estuvo bien en Anfield, nos va a dar mucho y esa parte está clara. Él está entrenando mucho para preparar el partido [se refería al derbi], tiene ilusión y va a hacer todo lo posible para estar", dijo en Movistar LaLiga. Y así es, Julián está listo y comprometido para el partido contra el Real Madrid: "Mañana. Todos. Juntos.".

articles.title: Man Utd: Have Eva Olid's WSL side shown signs of progress?
articles.summary: A week ago, the picture at Manchester United looked bleak. Then on Saturday, victory was snatched away from them at Arsenal. But have we seen signs of improvement from Eva Olid's side?
articles.body:
A week ago, the picture for Manchester United looked a lot bleaker than it did at the full-time whistle on Saturday.

Regardless of the stoppage-time equaliser they conceded at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, United's performance marked a major sign of progress.

Defeats in their opening two matches, including a 5-0 thrashing by Chelsea, meant the list of questions for new manager Eva Olid seemed endless.

United were disorganised, lacking in identity and were wide open at the back as their new era under Olid began in disappointing fashion.

Those early displays did little to fill supporters with confidence, and Olid faced criticism for her decisions despite being in the job just a matter of weeks.

However, a gutsy defensive display against Arsenal delivered a well-earned 1-1 draw and they were only denied victory by a 95th-minute leveller.

While United's wait for a first Women's Super League win of the season continues, this performance suggested there may not be quite the cause for concern many suspected.

Arsenal earn point with late leveller against Man Utd

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

Olid, 41, took over as manager in the summer, joining from Hearts, and promised to implement a new attacking style of play that focused heavily on possession.

However, in their opening two games, United had just two shots on target and less than 40% possession in both matches. In the second of those games, they suffered the five-goal humbling at home by Chelsea.

Few expected them to come away with anything against an Arsenal team who many tipped to win the title before the season kicked off, albeit they have struggled to score goals efficiently.

Olid knew it would be a test but said on Friday she wanted her players to believe in themselves, show confidence, and to go back to the defensive roots they knew and built so well under her predecessor Marc Skinner.

"It has been an intense week because there were a lot of emotions from players and staff. Nobody wants to lose 5-0," said Olid.

"We grew as a team. The first day after losing 5-0 is not easy for anyone. We spoke and said we needed energy this week and a positive mindset.

"The focus was the defensive shape. It's trying to get them more confidence."

Olid ultimately wants her United team to dominate the ball and create more chances in front of goal, but this time they delivered on her plea to be defensively solid.

They looked well organised in an even first half in which United midfielder Simi Awujo stood out, while Andrea Medina tracked back effectively.

They won more duels than Arsenal, put in more tackles and completed more interceptions than their opponents - but still had only 40% of possession.

Former England midfielder Izzy Christiansen told Sky Sports: "Manchester United have done a terrific job defensively. Overall, it's just been solid.

"It looks so much better. The addition of Awujo has added some running power and they look so much freer in the final third."

Arsenal's pressure grew in an edgy second half, but United held on for as long as they could and were unfortunate to concede with seconds left on the clock.

They had led from midway through the half, after Julia Zigiotti seized on a mistake from Georgia Stanway.

Smilla Holmberg's late volley denied United the spoils, but Olid saw foundations she could build on.

"I think the attacking will come," she said. "If you implement a new style of play, you need time.

"That effort, that intensity, can never be missed. We deserved three points for the hard work and the effort.

"Of course, we need to create more chances. That is why I'm here. We need time, but today is the minimum that we have to deliver. I hope we can improve the attacking side."

The biggest question is whether United really can build on this performance.

They were already a difficult team to break down under Skinner but came up short in previous big games against WSL title rivals.

In three Women's FA Cup finals, United won once against Tottenham, falling to higher-placed Chelsea on the other two occasions.

Four years have passed since they won a game at Emirates Stadium against Arsenal, and their heavy defeat by Chelsea last week showed the gap to the elite still remains.

Olid was brought in to transform their style by implementing an attacking philosophy that the club hope will deliver them long-term success.

Patience was already beginning to wane after their demoralising early defeats, so conversations took place and they had to revert back to what they already knew.

The result of that is significant progress from last week, but is it progress for the long term?

"We are a team who need to press high, but at the same time we want to be better with the ball," Olid said on Sky Sports.

"We lose simple passes and we cannot recognise the free player. Those things need to improve. It will come, I'm sure.

"But we need to keep this [defensive structure], then from there, little by little, be an attacking team, create more chances, score more goals.

"I cannot pretend it's happening in four weeks, but I'm sure it will come."

articles.title: Jay Dasilva's goal gives Coventry City Premier League win after over 25 years
articles.summary: Coventry City's win over Nottingham Forest - thanks to Jay Dasilva's goal - was a victory which was over 25 years in the making following some dark days for the Sky Blues.
articles.body:
Hear'Say were top of the pops, a mobile phone game called 'Snake' was all the rage and Tony Blair was Prime Minister.

Wind the clock back to April 2001 and things looked rather different.

It was also the last time Coventry City tasted victory in English football's top flight.

That came courtesy of a 1-0 win over Sunderland - John Hartson heading in the winner for Gordon Strachan's side in front of 20,946 fans at Highfield Road.

Much has happened in the life of Coventry since that moment 9,287 days ago. A rollercoaster journey might be understating it.

They were relegated at the end of the 2000-01 campaign and would spend the next 11 seasons in the second tier before dropping down to League One in 2012.

Then followed a particularly dark and turbulent period in the club's history featuring points deductions and a stint in administration.

Having left Highfield Road in 2005 they became embroiled in a bitter dispute over the Ricoh Arena in 2013 and its rent.

The nadir, arguably, was when they were forced to play matches away from Coventry, at Northampton Town, before later plummeting down to the fourth tier for the first time in 59 years in 2017.

Doubtless there were those packed into the Bridgford Stand at the City Ground on Saturday who were present during those years of Sky Blue hell.

So the explosion of emotion at the full-time whistle - after Jay Dasilva's goal settled matters - felt like Sky Blue heaven.

"It's been a tough opening for us, so those first Premier League points feel great," Coventry boss Frank Lampard told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"I thought the players were brilliant. The fight, work ethic and togetherness but also the tactical side of it. They dug and fought for each other which is what you need to win a Premier League game."

Coventry had been stranded on 99 Premier League wins for over a quarter of a century before this victory ticked them over to three figures at long last.

Lampard hopes this victory could be a key staging post in a campaign where avoiding relegation will be the main aim.

"It's really important for some of the players," he told BBC Match of the Day.

"For many of them it is their debut in the Premier League, they haven't been here before and they need to feel like they belong and play like that."

Lampard acknowledged his players must have thick skins to come through the slog of a Premier League season.

The fact this victory came off the back of a 5-0 drubbing at home to Brighton makes it all the more rewarding for the Coventry boss.

"There are lots of things we can learn and sometimes this year we may take those hits, it's a reality for teams that get to the Premier League," added Lampard.

"It's important we overcome them in terms of how we take it on board and stay together.

"It is easy to point in different directions when you lose but the group's really strong, really together, there'll have a good feeling from this one. But we'll keep our feet on the ground because it is one win, but it was needed for us."

articles.title: Barcelona sets asking price for Arsenal target ahead of January window
articles.summary: Arsenal are one of the teams ready to move if Barcelona open the door for Frenkie de Jong to leave, with the Gunners remaining keen to make a deal happen.Dur...
articles.body:
Arsenal are one of the teams ready to move if Barcelona open the door for Frenkie de Jong to leave, with the Gunners remaining keen to make a deal happen .

During the summer, De Jong was linked with a departure from Catalonia, but when that move failed to materialise, Arsenal signed Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United instead. The Gunners, however, remain attentive to opportunities to sign leading players, and De Jong is still viewed as an important target they could add to their squad during this window.

Arsenal now face competition from Liverpool , with the Reds also reportedly interested in the midfielder. According to Fichajes , Liverpool see De Jong as a player who could help address a major problem in their current midfield.

Arsenal will not want Liverpool to complete the deal, but Barcelona's position appears focused on the financial terms of any potential transfer. The Spanish club are reportedly prepared to allow De Jong to leave if a team meets their asking price for his signature.

The report states that Barcelona's new asking price is €73 million, with the club believing De Jong remains one of the best midfielders in the game despite his age and recent fitness problems.

The €73 million valuation could prove significant for the midfielder's suitors. Clubs interested in De Jong would likely consider that figure high, particularly given the recent concerns surrounding his fitness.

Barcelona are reportedly aware that their asking price could make negotiations more difficult, meaning there may be room for interested clubs to negotiate a lower fee. Arsenal could therefore continue monitoring the situation as they consider whether to make a move.

For now, De Jong remains a player who could attract significant attention if Barcelona decide to part ways with him.

articles.title: Watch Vanderbilt Score Walk-Off TD After NC State Botches Intentional Safety in End Zone
articles.summary: North Carolina State provided a textbook example of what not to do when trying to run out the clock and take an intentional safety to preserve a win.
articles.body:
North Carolina State provided a textbook example of what not to do when trying to run out the clock and take an intentional safety to preserve a win.

Holding a 31-28 lead over Vanderbilt with six seconds remaining, NC State quarterback CJ Bailey botched an attempt to run time off the clock, ran into a crowd of defenders and lost the ball in the end zone that was recovered by Vandy cornerback Cayden Daniels for the game-winning touchdown.

articles.title: Hibernian 1-1 Aberdeen: Martin Boyle penalty ends Hibs' home losing run with Scottish Premiership draw
articles.summary: Report as Hibernian end a run of six successive home defeats as Martin Boyle's second-half penalty earns the managerless hosts a 1-1 draw with Aberdeen in the Scottish Premiership after Kevin Nisbet's opener
articles.body:
The Dons went ahead in the 17th minute with a composed finish from former Hibs striker Kevin Nisbet.

Managerless Hibernian - with interim boss John Potter in charge following David Gray's midweek sacking - looked bereft of confidence for long spells.

However, the Leith side - who had previously lost six successive games at Easter Road - earned a share of the spoils after Boyle levelled from the penalty spot in the 62nd minute after Jack Milne dragged Jason Kerr to the ground.

There had been no meaningful attacking forays before Aberdeen stormed ahead through Nisbet.

Defender Gavin Molloy's ambitious shot from distance was mishit and fell to the Aberdeen captain in the box.

With his back to goal, Nisbet took one touch before planting a controlled shot past Rafa Sallinger from 12 yards.

That goal triggered a response from the hosts and they at least started exerting some pressure in the final third.

Dons goalkeeper Marius Muller made a near-post block to deny Owen Elding after the Irishman connected with Callum Wright's low ball into the six-yard box.

Miguel Chaiwa then lacked composure when a loose ball dropped to him 18 yards out and the midfielder lashed a half-volley well wide.

Aberdeen made a lively start to the second half and should have at least tested Sallinger with a breakaway in the 47th minute.

Afeez Aremu played in Toyosi Olusanya in the box but the angle was against the striker and he dragged a shot wide.

Hibs created a good chance of their own in the 54th minute when Felix Passlack found Josh Mulligan inside the area.

There were plenty of players in the midfielder's way and he scooped a harmless shot wide.

But Hibernian levelled in the 62nd minute courtesy of Boyle from the spot.

Aberdeen defender Milne had both arms around Kerr as the Hibs defender fell to the ground trying to get on the end of Adam Mayor's cross from a short corner.

Referee Nick Walsh pointed to the spot and Boyle sent his penalty straight down the middle.

Milne tried to make amends at the other end when he got on the end of Findlay Marshall's corner but yet his header was kept out on the line by Sallinger.

Home substitute Ante Suto then glanced a header wide at the back post after Wright flashed a cross into a dangerous area.

Hibs upped the pressure late on but could not find the winner.

articles.title: St Johnstone 1-1 Falkirk: Enes Alic stunner for 10-man Saints earns late Scottish Premiership draw
articles.summary: Report as Enes Alic scores a stunning 96th-minute free-kick to earn 10-man St Johnstone a dramatic 1-1 draw against Falkirk after Cheick Diabate's red card and Ethan Ross' opener
articles.body:
Falkirk took advantage of Cheick Diabate's 54th-minute red card to seize the lead through Ethan Ross on the hour.

And they looked sure to secure back-to-back William Hill Premiership wins until Taylor Steven won a late free-kick.

It was going to take something spectacular to beat Scott Bain, who had produced three fine saves for Falkirk.

But that is precisely what the Bosnian produced from 25 yards as he found the top corner to move Simo Valakari's side up to sixth place.

McDiarmid Park's East Stand was shut because of an electrical fault, forcing many home fans into the Geoff Brown and North Stands.

After a pre-match pledge to add goals to his improving game, St Johnstone winger Steven was twice foiled by Bain.

Reece McAlear's terrific ball over the top in the 19th minute found Josh Fowler and his deep cross picked out Steven, whose left-footed drive was met by a strong hand by the Scotland 'keeper as he tipped it over.

Saints struggled against the wind in the first half but McAlear judged his through-ball for Steven to perfection 15 minutes later, only for Bain to top his earlier stop by forcing Steven's shot on to the crossbar and away from danger.

Falkirk finished the first period the stronger side without greatly troubling Saints goalkeeper Toby Steward.

The on-loan Portsmouth 'keeper gathered efforts from Ryan Strain and Ross.

The best visiting chance came from a classy spin then pass from Ben Krauhaus splitting the Saints defence to send Jacob Murrell clear on Stewart, but he could not keep his shot down.

Diabate, booked in first-half stoppage time for a trip on Ross, dragged down the same player nine minutes into the second period and referee Calum Scott showed the former Exeter centre-back a second yellow card.

Valakari took off Josh Campbell to bring another defender, Daniel Finlayson, on.

But Falkirk had space to play with and that task was right up their street.

Owen Eames was sent speeding down the inside left channel and his clever cutback reached Ross on the edge of the box and he steered a superb first-time shot low into the far corner beyond Steward's reach.

That was the forward's first goal since the opening day of last season's Premiership campaign.

More inspired goalkeeping by Bain prevented substitute Ruari Paton from responding on the volley with 20 minutes to play.

The comeback bid appeared to have been hampered by a further defensive injury as Zach Mitchell was forced off.

Saints finished with a back three marshalled by Finlayson and refused to fold before conjuring a late leveller through Alic's moment of brilliance.

What the result means and next fixtures...
